page.layout: One page of running text, one column. No running head, no marginal notes. Printed page number at the head, catchword at the foot right.

main_text.p: atur ut (ng)vel ut vulgò [illegible, ~1 letter]; à Persis verò ut [illegible, ~1 letter], ut [illegible, ~2 letters] Gul rosa. Ideoque in in dicto Pentat. Persico, sæpius per [illegible, ~1 letter] effertur; quo etiam [illegible, ~1 letter] efferri solet.
Ordo literarum idem est Persis & Arabi-bus, & numerus etiam; exceptis quatuor [illegible, ~4 letters] quas Arabes non ha-bent.

Olim Hebræorum ordo observabatur, re-iectis ad finem literis asperioris soni, quod ex Epistolis Avicennæ Astrologicis, tum ex ipsius Canone medicinæ Romæ edito, lib.2, sen.2. ubi simplicia medicamenta secundum Hebræorum ordinem in Classes suas digeruntur; tum ex Euclidis propositionibus Arabicè editis, & ex tabulis omnibus, tum Persarum tum Arabum, Astronomicis, probat Doctissimus Joh. Gravius in Gram. Pers.p.9.10. Probabile autem est ad scripturæ venustatem, & ad sublevandam legendi & scribendi molestiam, ab iis qui pueros instituerunt, vel ab Alcorani scribis, consuetudinem hodiernam introductam fuisse.

page.notes: Arabic script throughout is partly illegible at this scan resolution; the Arabic letters are marked as illegible with approximate letter counts rather than guessed. The Persian word for rose ("Gul") is read with confidence; its Arabic-script form is not. The symbol after "vulgò" and the Arabic letter marks beside "effertur" and "etiam" are unreadable. The stain over "introductam" is slight; the reading is probable. Long s is rendered as a plain s throughout (e.g. "Persis", "rosa", "sen.2.", "Pers.p."). The page is headed by its printed number "(91.)" and the catchword "SECT." sits at the foot right.
